# Future-House/robin assessment

Source: [`Future-House/robin`](https://github.com/Future-House/robin) at [`4a5cce310f3bc7663a67117db88af43b84733ffe`](https://github.com/Future-House/robin/commit/4a5cce310f3bc7663a67117db88af43b84733ffe), dated 21 April 2026. The clean local ignored checkout was removed from `references/work/robin/` after assessment; it was never a runtime dependency. The root [Apache-2.0 license](https://github.com/Future-House/robin/blob/4a5cce310f3bc7663a67117db88af43b84733ffe/LICENSE) covers the repository. No separate component license file was tracked. Edison service access, model-provider terms, and generated or retrieved material are separate from that source license. No code, prompts, example outputs, or datasets have been copied. No upstream setup, tests, notebooks, or agent workflows have been executed.

## Implemented architecture and assumptions

- The importable package exposes [assay discovery, therapeutic-candidate discovery, and data analysis](https://github.com/Future-House/robin/blob/4a5cce310f3bc7663a67117db88af43b84733ffe/robin/__init__.py#L1-L12). [Assay discovery](https://github.com/Future-House/robin/blob/4a5cce310f3bc7663a67117db88af43b84733ffe/robin/assays.py#L27-L277) searches literature, proposes cell-culture assays, requests reports on them, compares them, and passes a selected assay into candidate generation. [Candidate discovery](https://github.com/Future-House/robin/blob/4a5cce310f3bc7663a67117db88af43b84733ffe/robin/candidates.py#L30-L169) searches and proposes therapeutic candidates, then requests detailed reports and ranks them. Prompts are in [`robin/prompts.py`](https://github.com/Future-House/robin/blob/4a5cce310f3bc7663a67117db88af43b84733ffe/robin/prompts.py).
- [Pairwise comparisons](https://github.com/Future-House/robin/blob/4a5cce310f3bc7663a67117db88af43b84733ffe/robin/utils.py#L422-L453) sample distinct pairs, capped at 300; [LLM judgments](https://github.com/Future-House/robin/blob/4a5cce310f3bc7663a67117db88af43b84733ffe/robin/utils.py#L584-L818) are aggregated with Choix ILSR. This is a different rating mechanism from the paper-backed local Elo tournament, not evidence of Google's internals.
- [Data analysis](https://github.com/Future-House/robin/blob/4a5cce310f3bc7663a67117db88af43b84733ffe/robin/analyses.py#L17-L202) obtains an Edison analysis and interprets its result into mechanistic insights, questions, and follow-up suggestions. [Candidate generation](https://github.com/Future-House/robin/blob/4a5cce310f3bc7663a67117db88af43b84733ffe/robin/candidates.py#L55-L69) can consume that interpreted result and [ask for new candidates](https://github.com/Future-House/robin/blob/4a5cce310f3bc7663a67117db88af43b84733ffe/robin/candidates.py#L148-L162), with [tested drugs called out in the prompt](https://github.com/Future-House/robin/blob/4a5cce310f3bc7663a67117db88af43b84733ffe/robin/prompts.py#L548-L557). This feedback handoff is the relevant external technique; its downstream scientific benefit is not measured here.
- [Edison task calls](https://github.com/Future-House/robin/blob/4a5cce310f3bc7663a67117db88af43b84733ffe/robin/utils.py#L70-L237) poll hosted tasks and save answers, task IDs, and references. The [multitrajectory runner](https://github.com/Future-House/robin/blob/4a5cce310f3bc7663a67117db88af43b84733ffe/robin/multitrajectory_runner.py#L104-L289) executes sequential steps and writes consolidated JSON after completion; the inspected code has no local durable checkpoint/resume contract. The [configuration](https://github.com/Future-House/robin/blob/4a5cce310f3bc7663a67117db88af43b84733ffe/robin/configuration.py#L242-L325) selects Edison CROW/FALCON tasks. The [README](https://github.com/Future-House/robin/blob/4a5cce310f3bc7663a67117db88af43b84733ffe/README.md#L5-L12) says Edison credits and a provider API key are needed. Both standard workflows call Edison, so the README's suggestion that generation runs without it is not an implemented fallback in the inspected paths.
- The checkout contains no tracked test suite. [Example-output directories](https://github.com/Future-House/robin/blob/4a5cce310f3bc7663a67117db88af43b84733ffe/README.md#L136-L163) are static snapshots, not repeatable acceptance tests. The RNA-seq prompt calls for `dea_results.csv`, while [`data_analysis()`](https://github.com/Future-House/robin/blob/4a5cce310f3bc7663a67117db88af43b84733ffe/robin/analyses.py#L54-L79) requests `flow_results.csv`. On a feedback rerun, [reports use an `_experimental` directory](https://github.com/Future-House/robin/blob/4a5cce310f3bc7663a67117db88af43b84733ffe/robin/candidates.py#L317-L336) but [ranking reads the original directory](https://github.com/Future-House/robin/blob/4a5cce310f3bc7663a67117db88af43b84733ffe/robin/candidates.py#L348-L379). These paths cannot establish reliable RNA-seq analysis or rerun ranking.

## Local comparison and candidate register

This register and the following assessment-time paragraphs preserve M10's original decision. The M11 implementation and releases are recorded below; only the campaign-owned live refinement observation remains unverified.

The local workbench already has evidence-grounded hypothesis generation, per-hypothesis pilot plans with controls and Go/No-Go criteria (`engine/src/co_scientist/agents/generation/experiment_plan.py`), reflection and specialist feedback (`engine/src/co_scientist/agents/evolution/evolve_feedback.py`), a persisted Elo tournament, and durable task recovery. Scientist-measured outcomes are append-only, bearer-owner scoped, and displayed separately from model conclusions (`app/app/store/outcomes.py`, `app/app/runs_contrib.py`, report and Ideas UI). They are not currently merged into continuation state (`app/app/engine_tasks_inputs.py`). This is a real workflow gap, but Robin's Edison analysis is not evidence that an arbitrary outcome is valid or that copying its prompt improves scientific quality.

| ID | Concrete gap and source mechanism | Local counterpart and fidelity | Reuse, boundary, disposition |
|---|---|---|---|
| M10-01 | A recorded experimental finding is visible but does not inform later hypothesis refinement. Robin [passes interpreted results into candidate generation](https://github.com/Future-House/robin/blob/4a5cce310f3bc7663a67117db88af43b84733ffe/robin/candidates.py#L55-L69). | Local append-only outcomes and scientist-input merge; **external technique/local design choice**, not a Google-backed requirement. | **Promising at M10 closure; independently implemented and released in PRs #43/#45.** The [M11 Robin feedback contract](robin/m11-feedback-contract.md) remains the frozen design; only the campaign-owned live observation, M11-ROBIN-01d4, is unverified. The selected design is one explicit owner-authorized outcome-to-linked-parent refinement, with bounded context, durable intent, lineage, disclosure, and unchanged review/safety/claim/Elo gates. No paid Edison, copied prompt, or automatic scoring. |
| M10-02 | A dedicated assay-search-and-selection stage can prioritize experiments before candidates. Robin [implements that sequence](https://github.com/Future-House/robin/blob/4a5cce310f3bc7663a67117db88af43b84733ffe/robin/assays.py#L88-L277). | Local hypothesis-specific experiment plans already give controls and decision thresholds, while the product remains a general research workbench rather than assay automation. | A separate cell-culture/drug-discovery mode is outside the campaign scope. A narrower actionable-planning gap would need evidence and safety validation; no source code copied. **Outside authorized scope for the separate stage.** |
| M10-03 | Robin prompts seek mechanistic specificity, target evidence, negative findings, safety and feasibility for therapeutic candidates ([prompt](https://github.com/Future-House/robin/blob/4a5cce310f3bc7663a67117db88af43b84733ffe/robin/prompts.py#L523-L589)). | Local generation, claims, reflection, safety, citations, experiment plan, and report already cover these axes for broader research goals. | **Already covered as criteria.** No additional untested prompt call or disease-specific restriction; any quality claim would require paired fixed-input evaluation. |
| M10-04 | Robin uses Choix aggregation for pairwise judgments ([implementation](https://github.com/Future-House/robin/blob/4a5cce310f3bc7663a67117db88af43b84733ffe/robin/utils.py#L584-L818)). | Local Google-backed Elo tournament and ranking-concordance evaluator. | **Rejected for direct replacement:** the source has no tracked comparative tests or expert-outcome evidence showing a benefit, while replacement would break documented fidelity. No added model cost or dependency. |
| M10-05 | Edison task IDs, polling and file reports support trajectories ([runner](https://github.com/Future-House/robin/blob/4a5cce310f3bc7663a67117db88af43b84733ffe/robin/multitrajectory_runner.py#L104-L289)). | Local SQLite task leases/checkpoints/recovery and provenance already cover durable research execution. | **Already covered for this product;** paid Edison and a second runtime are outside authorized scope. Static inspection cost zero; no hosted experiment was run. |

At M10 source assessment, the campaign's only potential adoption was M10-01. A read-only independent review found the safest candidate shape to be an explicit follow-up action on one outcome, with the observation kept distinct from the researcher's interpretation and with context attached only to the linked hypothesis. Auto-including all outcomes in global preferences would keep sensitive or stale text in generation, ranking and other prompts; converting an outcome into a scored review would falsely promote measurement to judgment. The current steering scheduler forces **generation**, while the ordinary evolution ledger selects only the top five rankable parents, so neither existing route guarantees that an owner-selected outcome reaches its linked parent. [M11-ROBIN-01a freezes the explicit action, fixed public case, eligibility, context bound, disclosure, durable intent, lineage, gate separation, acceptance boundary, and limits](robin/m11-feedback-contract.md). The later M11 implementation passed targeted-route, restart/idempotency and accessible-UI checks; no scientific-quality improvement, wet-lab validation or full live run is claimed.

## Free-route boundary during this assessment

The [24 September official catalog receipt](robin/m10-free-route-2026-09-24.json) still lists the selected exact Nex Pro route at zero prompt and completion price, with a 25 September expiry date. A fresh non-secret Railway production readback found `MODEL_NAME`, `SUPERVISOR_MODEL_NAME`, `CHAT_MODEL_NAME`, and `SEMANTIC_SAFETY_MODEL` all set to `openrouter/nex-agi/nex-n2.5-pro:free`; `CLAIM_VERIFIER_MODEL` is unset and inherits it. The request boundary rechecks exact route prices and applies zero-price caps. The M9 browser probe was stopped during streamed reasoning and recorded neither terminal response nor served-model metadata; it cannot establish a terminal-answer defect. Earlier retained [actual app-stream evidence](baseline/model-qualification/README.md) for Nex Pro did reach ten content deltas and a `stop` with observed served model and usage. That is capability evidence, not a production interview or end-to-end research report. No new model call or deployment was made for M10 source assessment. The route's advertised retirement is retained as M11-OPS-02: later inference must first recheck current prices and production configuration, with no paid or unqualified fallback. [NVIDIA's free Nemotron page](https://openrouter.ai/nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free) warns against confidential information or personal data, so catalog price and interface support alone do not justify making it the default for private user research.

## Verification and release

No product mechanism was accepted at the M10 source release; its M11 implementation and UI were released later in PRs #43/#45, while live M11-ROBIN-01d4 remains unverified. The source and local comparison used static inspection only. `git diff --check` passed and the existing offline safety/citation smoke passed against the current worktree using the local Python environment. Full code, UI and scientific-quality evaluations were not run for a documentation-only change; no improvement in generated hypotheses or experimental validity is claimed. Scoped cleanup found no new code, duplicate runtime, dead branch or UI change, and removed the clean temporary checkout from `references/work/`.

[PR #39](https://github.com/guy915/Co-Scientist/pull/39) merged the assessment as `640d75ee9f2e0297888494f0cd64adf1a9f15ef0`. GitHub-hosted CI was waived by the user when its required affected-targets job failed without a runner log; this was not reported as a passing check. The main push nevertheless caused existing-service builds: Railway API `b502644d-8164-44ed-bbdb-61ecc50390d7`, Railway MCP `803a055f-f075-4784-ae82-2dfe805426fc`, and Vercel production `dpl_G8ysjs9CTuhMuiA8tyRgHYMwUmbu` all reached healthy terminal states on that commit. The public frontend alias points to the Vercel deployment. After both Railway deployments succeeded, non-mutating production smoke passed all five checks. API configuration still has one replica, the `/app/data` volume, root UID, off-volume cache, and four explicit Nex Pro model roles with no separate verifier override. No campaign inference, production data mutation, paid service, or manual redeploy was involved.

## M11 implementation follow-up

M10-01 was accepted as an **external technique implemented independently**, not as a Google-backed requirement or a copy of Robin code. The action is explicit: a researcher records an append-only observation, then separately requests refinement of that outcome's linked parent hypothesis. The API freezes one owner-bound, at-most-6,000-code-point context with at most three attributed source metadata links. It creates a stable outbox/task key, restores the same action after restart, and exposes owner-scoped status reads. The executor calls the existing evolution operator for that parent only; siblings are available solely for duplicate validation. The child carries outcome→parent→child lineage and traverses the ordinary review, claim, safety and Elo path. The observation does not become a claim verdict, safety verdict or rating. The workbench discloses the model handoff and shows saved status/retry through completed, active and failed run views. The action uses the existing provider/free-price admission boundary and introduces no Edison dependency or second runtime.

Local acceptance evidence includes red-first API ownership/idempotency tests, provider-failure and restart recovery, checkpoint redelivery without a second child, one-parent context isolation, a normal gate-path test and a Playwright active/failed refresh regression. The full pre-release app, engine, MCP, parity, lint, type, build, evaluation-smoke, frontend and existing browser suites passed; the new browser regression passed separately after the UI correction. The [consistent pre-migration backup manifest](robin/m11-production-backup.json) records verification without retaining production rows. No live scientific-quality improvement or wet-lab validity is inferred from these software tests.

[PR #43](https://github.com/guy915/Co-Scientist/pull/43) merged the implementation as `8dcb4280` under the user's explicit hosted-CI waiver. The [release record](robin/m11-release-verification.json) retains exact deployment IDs and checks: Railway API/MCP reached SUCCESS, Vercel reached READY on the merge commit, and production smoke passed 5/5. The API retains one replica, its volume-backed database and off-volume cache, root UID for volume access, and the embedded worker. The official catalog still listed the deployed Nex Pro route at zero prompt/completion price at the release check, with same-day advertised retirement; no campaign inference was made. M11-ROBIN-01d4 remains open because a live refinement on a completed campaign-owned production run has not been observed. The local fixed-public-case boundary is verified; the scientific-quality claim remains deliberately absent.
